data.narrative:
Cortical Labs is a Series A-stage AI & Software company founded by Hon Weng Chong and Andy Kitchen that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public peer company (Palantir), with primary focus on 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers: Reflection AI ($25.0B Series A), Together AI ($8.3B Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B Series B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B Series B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression uses the $11M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for Series A advancement, implying a $22M valuation. Peer-Median compares Cortical Labs against the 4-company cohort, which exhibits a median valuation of $7.0B (range: $3.2B to $25.0B), reflecting the current heterogeneity of AI & Software valuations at comparable development stages.

The triangulated analysis yields a range of $19M (low) to $8.0B (high), with a median of $3.5B. The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects fundamental uncertainty around Cortical Labs' relative technical capability and market positioning within a volatile frontier-AI sector. Resolution of this range depends critically on near-term technical milestones, revenue traction, and whether the company's performance trajectory aligns more closely with the distributed-AI or foundational-model segments of the peer set.
